eng.titles: The Party · The Heroes · Moscow · The Sheep · The Trip · The F-14s
eng.expect: The Shah falls and the joy curdles fast. Marji meets the released prisoners (Siamak, Mohsen) and hears about torture; her uncle Anoosh arrives from Moscow with the family's political past; the new regime starts executing the very people who fought the Shah; the family tries a holiday abroad; then the war with Iraq begins and the F-14s fly over Tehran.
eng.watch: How Satrapi draws a child understanding adult horror: the torture panel drawn like a diagram; the black page after Anoosh; crowds as identical silhouettes; the shift from celebration panels to empty ones. Note every time the verbal text is calm while the image is not.
eng.questions: 1) Where does the narrator's adult voice interrupt the child's view, and what does that gap create? 2) What does 'hero' mean to Marji before and after these chapters?
eng.globalIssues: Politics, power and justice (revolution eating its children) · Beliefs, values and education (heroism as a story children are told)
eng.quotes: Look for the lines about Anoosh's photograph, the swan he carves, and 'the heroes' that Marji wants in her own family.

eng.titles: The Jewels · The Key · The Wine · The Cigarette · The Passport · Kim Wilde
eng.expect: Wartime daily life: shortages and fights over food, the plastic keys to paradise given to poor boys sent to the front, secret parties and wine, Marji's first rebellion (the cigarette), her uncle's failed passport, and the black-market Kim Wilde tape that gets her stopped by the Guardians of the Revolution.
eng.watch: Contrast as argument: the boys with keys exploding on the minefield drawn on the same page as Marji's party. The veil scenes; the Guardians drawn as identical shapes. How humor is used inside horror, and what it protects.
eng.questions: 1) How does the regime reach into private life, and how do the images show the private/public split? 2) Is Marji's rebellion political or adolescent, and does the book let us decide?
eng.globalIssues: Culture, identity and community (Western culture as resistance) · Politics, power and justice (class and who dies in the war)
eng.quotes: The key to paradise; 'the cigarette' as a declaration of independence; the punk badge and the Nike shoes.

eng.titles: The Shabbat · The Dowry · The Soup · Tyrol · Pasta · The Pill
eng.expect: The missile hits the neighbours' house and the Baba-Levy family; Marji's confrontations at school; the story of Niloufar and why a virgin cannot be executed; her parents send her to Vienna. Then exile begins: a boarding house run by nuns, a new language, loneliness, and a first friend group of outsiders.
eng.watch: The single most famous page of the book: the black panel of the missile and the bracelet. How the drawing style changes when Marji is alone in Austria (more white space, smaller figures). The 'dowry' chapter's understatement.
eng.questions: 1) What is the effect of Satrapi refusing to draw the body in the rubble? 2) How does exile change the relationship between text and image?
eng.globalIssues: Culture, identity and community (exile, belonging) · Politics, power and justice (the dowry scene: law as violence)
eng.quotes: 'No scream in the world could have relieved my suffering'; the dowry money; the first Austrian bathroom scene.

eng.titles: The Vegetable · The Horse · Hide and Seek · The Croissant · The Veil
eng.expect: Vienna years: Marji changes her body, her friends, her name for herself; the flat with the mad landlady; first love and its collapse; homelessness and illness; and finally the return to Tehran, where the veil comes back on.
eng.watch: Body as a drawn argument (growth panels, the mirror). Satrapi's honesty about her own failures. The last page of the section: the veil as both prison and home.
eng.questions: 1) What does Marji lose in freedom that she had in Tehran? 2) How does the book treat shame?
eng.globalIssues: Culture, identity and community (identity between two cultures) · Art, creativity and imagination (the self as a drawn character)
eng.quotes: The chapter title irony of 'The Vegetable'; the sequence of 'I was a Westerner in Iran, an Iranian in the West'.

eng.titles: The Return · The Joke · Skiing · The Exam · The Makeup
eng.expect: Back in Tehran with the war's traces on every street; depression and a suicide attempt told with startling flatness; then reinvention: aerobics, makeup, the university entrance exam, art school under religious rules.
eng.watch: How the book narrates despair without melodrama; the 'joke' chapter's dark humour; the exam and the drawing class with the veiled model as commentary on art under censorship.
eng.questions: 1) Why does Satrapi tell the darkest moment so briefly? 2) What does 'the makeup' chapter say about performance and survival?
eng.globalIssues: Art, creativity and imagination (art under censorship) · Beliefs, values and education
eng.quotes: The martyrs' street names; the anatomy class; the line about wanting to be 'a liberated and emancipated woman'.

eng.titles: The Convocation · The Socks · The Wedding · The Satellite · The End
eng.expect: University life under morality police, the marriage that she knows is a mistake, satellite dishes and the parties that follow, the last years before she leaves Iran for good. The book closes on her departure and her grandmother.
eng.watch: The lecture on the veil where Marji speaks back; the wedding page composition; the final farewell and what the last panel withholds.
eng.questions: 1) Is the ending an escape or a loss, and how does the image decide it? 2) Which single frame would you choose for an IO and why?
eng.globalIssues: Politics, power and justice · Culture, identity and community (the final departure)
eng.quotes: 'Freedom had a price'; the grandmother's last advice; the airport.

port.expect: Um cartum inédito e a pergunta: como a autora combina os elementos verbais e visuais para construir significados? Você terá 75 minutos e a resposta é um texto analítico estruturado, não uma dissertação de opinião.
port.watch: Enquadramento e ângulo; traço (grosso/fino, caricatura); uso do preto e branco ou cor; balões, legendas e tipografia; ironia entre o que se diz e o que se vê; o alvo da crítica; intertexto com notícias; o silêncio (o que não é dito).
port.questions: 1) Qual é o efeito de cada escolha, e não apenas o nome dela? 2) Onde o verbal contradiz o visual?
port.globalIssues: Política, poder e justiça · Cultura, identidade e comunidade
port.quotes: Zero repertório externo · zero proposta de intervenção · zero 'é notório que'. Tese na primeira frase, três parágrafos escolha→efeito→sentido, conclusão com 'e daí?'.

phys-test-0925.title: Physics · A.2 forces only
phys-test-0925.expect: Free-body diagrams, Newton's three laws, resolving forces on inclines, friction (static vs kinetic, μ), tension and pulleys, normal force, weight vs mass, equilibrium, terminal velocity qualitatively. Probably a mix of MCQ and short structured questions with a data-booklet formula sheet.
phys-test-0925.traps: Axes not aligned with the incline · forgetting the normal force changes on a slope · using μ·N with the wrong N · sign errors when the net force is zero · units and significant figures on the final answer.
phys-test-0925.do: Draw the diagram before touching a formula. State the principle, write the equation, substitute, box the answer with a unit.

port-test-0925.title: Português · Paper 1 (cartum)
port-test-0925.expect: Um cartum (provavelmente Duke ou Carol Ito) e a pergunta-guia sobre elementos verbais e visuais. 75 minutos, ~900–1100 palavras.
port-test-0925.traps: Descrever em vez de analisar · nomear recursos sem efeito · fugir para o assunto do cartum em vez do texto · conclusão-resumo.
port-test-0925.do: 10 minutos de plano: tese + três escolhas com efeito. Cada parágrafo termina em 'o que faz o leitor...'.

chem-test-1009.title: Chem · Structure 1 (S1.1–S1.5)
chem-test-1009.expect: States and changes of state, mixtures and separation; the nuclear atom, isotopes, mass spectra; electron configurations, emission spectra, orbitals and Aufbau; the mole, empirical and molecular formulae, solutions and concentration; ideal gases and pV = nRT with unit conversions. Expect calculations to be most of the marks.
chem-test-1009.traps: Mole calculations with wrong units (dm³ vs cm³, kPa vs Pa) · empirical formula rounding · electron configuration exceptions (Cr, Cu) · significant figures.
chem-test-1009.do: One mixed practice set per day from Sep 25; full timed paper Oct 5–6; error-only pass Oct 7; light Oct 8.
